title: STAR WARS: Galactic Racer
provenance: Reported by DanielAdomian (highball-db#1058, 2026-11-07), Apple , macOS , engine , , rated  of 5. Not verified by the maintainer. DanielAdomian again on highball-db#1058 (2026-11-08), +loaddll logs on the Wine 11 engines r30 and r28 (D3DMetal, the Games environment): r31 fails the same way, and Highball shows the game as running for a few seconds. Before the end SWGR-Win64-Shipping.exe queries nearly every system, process and thread information class in a shuffled order, many of which Wine doesn't answer, which looks like a fingerprinting pass. The c0000409 address lies inside Steam's overlay DLL, gameoverlayrenderer64.dll, at offset 0xdea75 in both logs, and the first log's address ends the same way. An earlier reply said it sat in one of Wine's DLLs, which was wrong.
notes: Doesn't start yet in one report on an M1 Mac mini: the game ends itself right after starting, before it opens a window, on the Wine 10 and Wine 11 engines. The Steam release carries Denuvo Anti-Tamper (store page).

knownIssues.symptom: Exits right after starting, before any window (M1, Wine 10 engines and Wine 11 r28, r30 and r31)
knownIssues.cause: not diagnosed. Right after the game's sweep of system, process and thread information queries, many of which Wine doesn't answer, exception c0000409, the code a Windows program uses to stop itself at once, is raised from inside Steam's overlay DLL gameoverlayrenderer64.dll (offset 0xdea75 in every log), before any graphics device exists, so the graphics mode isn't involved (the reporter's +loaddll traces, highball-db#1058)
knownIssues.fix: none known. Untested: turning the Steam overlay off for the game

knownIssues.symptom: Epic Online Services fails to install on the Wine 10 engines (SetNamedSecurityInfo error 120, MSI error 1603)
knownIssues.cause: error 120 means the call isn't implemented, a Windows security call Wine 10 lacks for what the installer asks (the reporter's reading)
